- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment for bullish bias — if sentiment is weak or mixed, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., <10% under 3–5 days), sentiment is often bearish — increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment turns neutral or bullish.
- Model tends to lag in early days of sentiment shift — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change if sentiment is trending.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extreme outliers (e.g., >15% above or below mean) unless sentiment strongly supports it — use sentiment as filter for outlier rejection.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/0.67), model often overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
